newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Paper sees difficult H1.
newsitem.headline: FCL Paper sees difficult H1.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Aug 28 (Reuter) Fletcher Challenge paper said on Wednesday that conditions for printing papers and market pulp were expected to remain dificult for at least the first half of the current year to June, 1997.
But FCL Paper said it believed the current weakness in demand was temporary in nature as producers and publishers balanced their inventories better.
"Stronger growth in key world economies and an end to destocking are expected to lead to an improvement in market conditions during 1997," it said.
FCL Paper earlier reported a NZ$177 million net profit for the year to June, 1996, up three percent on the previous year.
Operating earnings for publication papers were NZ$461 million, substantially up from $175 million in the 1995 fiscal year.
Demand for newsprint was strong in the first six months of the year, partly due to inventory buildup.
But prices had begun to move lower by last December and by June 1996 had declined by 11 percent.

Chief Executive John Hood said although the financial performance over the second half of 1996 had been poor, the company remained in good financial condition. Debt to capitalisation remained conservative at 32 percent.
A 3.0 NZ cent dividend had been declared based on expectations of an improvement over the next 24 months.
